h1: The 7 Best Cordless Phones for Small Businesses, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Small Business Cordless Phones: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 DECT 6.0 cordless phone systems for small offices, scored on handsets, line support, conferencing and scam blocking.
summary: The AT&T DLP73590 is the best small-office cordless system, with five handsets, conference calling and a 5 inch color display. The VTech IS8151-5 is the pick for a growing team because it expands to 12 handsets and has a headset jack and power backup. Panasonic's KX-TGF975B is the call-screening specialist, and the AT&T TL88102BK is the only true two-line system.
intro: The first question for a small business is not how many handsets you need, but how many phone lines. Most cordless phones sold for homes are single-line, which means one person can be on a call and everyone else gets a busy tone, no matter how many handsets are lying around. More handsets give you more places to answer, not more capacity to talk. If two people regularly need to be on outside calls at the same time, you want a two-line system, or a cordless that plugs into a phone service with several lines.

We ranked seven DECT 6.0 systems around that distinction. We reviewed listings for handset count, line support, conference calling, scam protection, headset support, expandability and backup power. DECT 6.0 phones run on their own radio band, so they avoid the Wi-Fi interference older cordless phones suffered from. Where a listing is silent on a feature, we say so and leave it out.

products.name: AT&T 5-Handset DECT 6.0 Cordless Home and Business Phone with Answering Machine, 5" Color Display, One-Touch Shortcut, Conference, Intercom, Smart Call Blocker, Bluetooth Connect to Cell - DLP73590
products.verdict: Five handsets, conference calling and a 5 inch color display in one office-ready system.
products.description:
The DLP73590 comes with five handsets, a 5 inch color display, conference calling, an intercom, a built-in answering machine and a smart call blocker. It also pairs with a cell phone over Bluetooth, and it carries a one-touch shortcut key.

It ranks first because it covers the whole small-office checklist in one box. Conference calling lets two handsets join the same outside call, which is useful for a quick three-way talk with a client. The intercom links handsets without using the phone line. Bluetooth cell connection lets you answer a mobile call on a desk handset, which suits owners who give out a mobile number. Its limit is that it is still a single-line phone, so two people cannot take separate outside calls at once.

Buy it for an office of up to five people with one main number. If two calls often overlap, look at the two-line AT&T TL88102BK.
pros: Five handsets cover a small office
cons: Single line, so one call at a time
products.idealFor: Small offices that want conference calling and a color display across five handsets.
products.skipIf: You need two simultaneous outside calls.

products.name: VTech IS8151-5 Super Long Range 5 Handset DECT 6.0 Cordless Phone for Home with Answering Machine, 2300 ft Range, Call Blocking, Bluetooth, Headset Jack, Power Backup, Intercom, Expandable to 12 HS
products.verdict: Expands to 12 handsets, with a headset jack, power backup and a claimed 2300 ft range.
products.description:
The IS8151-5 includes five handsets and can be expanded to 12. The listing claims a 2300 ft range and lists call blocking, Bluetooth, an answering machine, an intercom, a headset jack and power backup.

It takes second place because it is the one that can keep growing. Adding handsets as you hire is cheaper than replacing the system, and a headset jack lets staff who spend hours on calls work hands-free. Power backup keeps the phones running through a short outage, which matters for a business that cannot go dark. The 2300 ft range is a best-case open-air claim; walls and metal shelving will cut it sharply. It trails the AT&T only because the listing does not mention conference calling.

Choose it for a team that is still growing or a larger building. Expect real-world range to be much shorter than the claim.
cons: Range claim is open-air best case
products.idealFor: Growing offices that need headset support and expansion beyond five handsets.

products.name: AT&T 4-Handset DECT 6.0 Cordless Home and Business Phone with Answering Machine, 5" Color Display, One-Touch Shortcut, Conference, Intercom, Smart Call Blocker, Bluetooth Connect to Cell - DLP73490
products.verdict: The same feature set as the leader with four handsets instead of five.
products.description:
The DLP73490 is the four-handset version of the top pick, with the same 5 inch color display, conference calling, intercom, smart call blocker and Bluetooth cell connection.

It ranks third because the only difference from the DLP73590 is the number of handsets, and that matters just to some buyers. If your team is four people or fewer, you save money by skipping the fifth handset. If you might hire, the five-handset kit costs little more and avoids a mismatch later. All the functional benefits of the top pick carry over, including the same single-line limit.

Buy it for an office of exactly four people with one shared line. Pick the five-handset version if the team might grow.
pros: Same features as the five-handset kit
products.idealFor: Small offices with exactly four staff needing business features.
products.skipIf: You may add a fifth person soon.

products.name: Panasonic Cordless Phone with Answering Machine, Advanced Call Block, Link2Cell Bluetooth, One-Ring Scam Alert, 2-Way Recording, Spam/Robocall Protection and 5 Handsets - KX-TGF975B
products.verdict: Advanced call blocking, one-ring scam alerts and two-way recording across five handsets.
products.description:
The KX-TGF975B includes five handsets, advanced call blocking, a one-ring scam alert, two-way recording and spam and robocall protection, plus Link2Cell Bluetooth and an answering machine.

It ranks fourth because it leans toward call screening instead of conferencing. One-ring scam alert flags the pattern of a single ring from an unfamiliar number, and the advanced block keeps known nuisance callers off the line. Two-way recording captures a conversation, which can help with order details, though recording laws vary by state and you should tell the other party. Link2Cell connects a cell phone so you can answer mobile calls on the handsets.

Choose it if your business fields many unfamiliar callers or suffers spam. Without conference calling in the listing, a small team that holds three-way calls should look at the AT&T.
cons: Recording needs consent in many states
products.idealFor: Businesses that field many unfamiliar calls and want advanced scam protection.

products.name: AT&T TL88102BK DECT 6.0 2-Line Expandable Cordless Phone with Answering System and Dual Caller ID/Call Waiting, 3 Handsets, Black
products.verdict: The only real two-line cordless system here, with dual caller ID and an answering system.
products.description:
The TL88102BK is a two-line expandable DECT 6.0 system with three handsets, an answering system and dual caller ID and call waiting. It sits in the $200 to $500 price band.

It ranks fifth because two-line capability is a feature that suits fewer businesses. Two lines mean two people can take separate outside calls at once, or one line can stay free for a fax or a second number. Dual caller ID shows who is calling on each. It costs more than the five-handset kits and includes only three handsets, and the listing does not mention conferencing, Bluetooth or call blocking. For a business with two lines, though, nothing else in this list does the job.

Buy it if you have two phone lines and need both reachable at once. Skip it if you have one line, since you are paying for a feature you cannot use.
pros: Dual caller ID and call waiting
products.idealFor: Small businesses that need genuine dual-line management, not just more handsets.
products.skipIf: You only have one phone line.

products.name: AT&T BL102-4 DECT 6.0 4-Handset Cordless Phone for Home with Answering Machine, Call Blocking, Caller ID Announcer, Audio Assist, Intercom, and Unsurpassed Range
products.verdict: Four handsets with call blocking, caller ID announcer and an intercom for less.
products.description:
The BL102-4 gives you four handsets plus an intercom, with a built-in answering machine, a caller ID announcer that speaks the name aloud, audio assist and number blocking. It costs between $100 and $200.

It ranks sixth because it is the stripped-down choice. Call blocking handles nuisance numbers, the announcer reads out who is calling so you can screen without looking, and audio assist boosts volume in noisy rooms. There is no conference calling or color display. For an office that just needs to answer a phone from several rooms, that is perfectly adequate.

Buy it if you want a clean, simple multi-handset system without paying for conferencing. Skip it if three-way calls or a bigger display matter to your staff.
pros: Four handsets for a modest price
Caller ID announcer speaks the name
products.idealFor: Small offices that want call blocking and intercom without paying for conference calling.
products.skipIf: You want three-way calls or a color display.

products.name: Gigaset Comfort 552A Trio, 3 Cordless Phones, Answering Machine, Made in Germany, Elegant Design, Hands-Free Mode, Comfort Call Protection, Big Phone Book, Titanium-Black
products.verdict: A three-handset European-designed set with hands-free mode and a big phone book.
products.description:
The Gigaset Comfort 552A Trio includes three cordless phones and an answering machine, with a hands-free mode, comfort call protection and a big phone book. The listing says it is made in Germany, and it costs between $50 and $100.

It ranks last because it is designed for a household more than an office. The big phone book helps if you store many client numbers, and hands-free mode helps when you need both hands. The design stands out against the usual black plastic of the AT&T line. But three handsets, no conferencing and no explicit headset or expansion detail limit its use for a growing business.

Choose it if you run a very small office, such as a home business, and value a distinctive design at a lower price. Otherwise, one of the larger kits fits better.
pros: Lower price than the larger kits
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a European-designed alternative at a lower price.
products.skipIf: You plan to grow past three staff.

whatMatters.detail: A single-line system allows one outside call at a time, no matter how many handsets it has. A two-line system supports two separate calls at once. Check the listing for 2-line, and decide whether two people ever need to be on outside calls at the same moment.

Included handsets set your starting capacity, and expandability lets you add more later. Buying a system that expands avoids replacing the base when you hire. Look for a maximum handset number, such as 12.

Conference calling lets two handsets join the same outside call, and intercom lets handsets call each other without using the line. Both are useful in an office, and not every cordless system includes them. Check the listing for the words conference and intercom.

Call blocking lets the phone reject numbers you choose, and some models flag suspicious patterns such as a single ring. For a business that answers calls from unknown numbers, this saves time. Look for named features, not just a general claim of blocking.

Range claims are measured in open air, so walls and equipment reduce them sharply. Power backup keeps the phones working during an outage if the base can run on batteries. Treat range numbers as ceilings, and check whether backup power is included.

faq.q: Will these phones work with a VoIP service?
faq.a: Most DECT 6.0 phones connect to a standard phone jack, so they work with VoIP only if the VoIP adapter provides a phone port. Check how your provider connects to the building. Bluetooth cell linking is an alternative for mobile numbers.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake small businesses make?
faq.a: Buying more handsets when they need more lines. Handsets add places to answer, not capacity to talk. If callers get a busy tone, a two-line system or a VoIP service is the fix.

faq.q: Is a business cordless worth it over a home cordless?
faq.a: It is if you need conference calling, an intercom, headset support or two lines. Many home models lack those. If you only need to answer from a few rooms, a home model like the AT&T BL102-4 is enough.

faq.q: How do I set up additional handsets?
faq.a: Place the new handset on its charger, then register it to the base with the pairing menu or button. The process takes a few minutes. Check the maximum number of handsets the base supports.

The Panasonic KX-TGF975B lists two-way recording, but recording laws vary, and some states require everyone on the call to consent. Tell callers when you are recording. Check your local rules before relying on it.

faq.q: How long do the handset batteries last?
faq.a: Cordless phone batteries usually last a few years before talk time falls. Replace them with the type the manual specifies. Keeping handsets on their chargers when idle is normal.

finalTake: The AT&T DLP73590 is the best cordless phone for most small businesses, thanks to five handsets, conference calling and a Bluetooth cell link. The VTech IS8151-5 is the better choice if you expect to grow or need headsets. Panasonic suits those who drown in spam calls, and the AT&T TL88102BK is the only option here for two real phone lines.
